customManagers.description: Bump the node-version input passed to the shared claude-config ci-npm.yml reusable workflow. The github-actions manager only sees setup-node with: blocks, so this caller input was left behind on Node majors (web #440 / admin #180 bumped the Dockerfile to 26 while CI checks still ran on 24). Datasource node-version + depName node puts it in the same Node PR as the Dockerfile bump.

packageRules.description: Never automerge major GitHub Actions bumps — review them
Group non-major Go module updates into one PR

Batch the renovate-config-validator pre-commit hook weekly. renovatebot/pre-commit-hooks mirrors the near-daily Renovate release train, so with no schedule it produced a self-merging PR most days (only email-service pins it). One grouped PR on Mondays instead. minimumReleaseAge (3 days) and the infra-automerge rule above still apply.
Do not pin first-party claude-config reusable workflows to a digest — same org/trust boundary, and pinning only adds cross-repo bump churn. Callers track @main directly.

Group the whole GraphQL stack (graphql + graphql-request + graphql-tag + every @graphql-codegen/* plugin) into one PR. A graphql major (e.g. v17) cannot resolve until the codegen toolchain and graphql-request peer-accept it, so a lone graphql bump just sits red. Grouping puts the set in one branch that Renovate re-tests whenever ANY member updates — so when the lagging packages (graphql-request, @graphql-codegen/typescript-graphql-request) finally ship a compatible release, the same PR rebases and its CI (npm ci + codegen + typecheck) re-runs and goes green only once the versions are mutually compatible. The PR self-greens when the ecosystem aligns — no manual version pin to track and lift. Used by the Nuxt apps (web, admin).
